change.origin: Issue #649 lists four log probe hardening items from the PR #622 review. The driver is accepted at 82fe22a0a (digest 4bc13454). Thirteen later commits on dev changed the driver or its fixture without a new acceptance, and no gate detected it (issue #777). This package therefore covers the full change from 82fe22a0a to da4e39458.
issue_649: The node log docker exec gets /dev/null as its standard input, so a later change cannot consume the container ID list.
An empty LogPath makes the probe unavailable with the reason 'the logging driver writes no log file'.
The probe error file is a mktemp file in TMPDIR. An EXIT trap in the guardian removes it. Nothing is written to OUTPUT_DIR.
SOAK_NODE_LOG_DIR sets the node log directory (default /var/lib/rnode/logs). A value that is not an absolute path of letters, digits, '.', '_', '-', and '/' stops the driver with exit 2.

unaccepted_changes_since_82fe22a0a.change: After a fixture exit 2, report the scenario, the driver exit code, the summary state, and the last 20 driver log lines. SOAK_DISK_TEST_DRIVER_TIMEOUT overrides the driver timeout (TASK-023-2).
The log-probe-vanished workload ends after the vanish and one later probe, not after a fixed 25 s sleep (TASK-023-1).
session_bounded kills its watchdog by PID when the process group kill fails, because the watchdog may not have called setsid yet. Before, wait blocked for the full watchdog budget (TASK-023-8).
session_bounded tries the group kill again after the PID kill. The fixture counts LogPath probes with a default of 0 when the command file does not exist yet.
During work, one failed log probe is a warning. Two consecutive failed probes are a breach. The admission check still refuses on one failure (weekend soak 38076682321).
The node log probe keeps the stdout and the stderr of docker exec apart. It parses stdout only after a zero exit status, and it accepts only one '<bytes>\t<directory>' line (PR #698 review).
The fixture creates ci-ports.shard.yml, matches the new compose arguments, and returns a validator1 port in the merged config.
Each iteration can start the node I/O sampler (scripts/bench/sample-node-io.sh) for issue #24.
The repository variable SOAK_IO_DIAGNOSTICS gates the I/O sampler, which is off by default.
An iteration that the segment deadline stops (exit 124) is not recorded as a provider failure in its metrics.
The driver compresses each iteration's node-metrics CSV with gzip when the snapshot loop stops, and skips it under an emergency deadline (weekend run 38995239992 stopped on the disk floor).
The gzip step runs after the I/O sampler stops. A gzip failure is logged, and the soak continues (PR #759 review).
Each iteration writes issue24-phases.jsonl next to metrics.json (PR #767).

change.fixture: Three new scenarios in scripts/bench/test-soak-disk-admission.sh: log-probe-no-logfile-boundary, log-node-dir-override, and log-node-dir-range. The in-budget scenarios check that each node log exec gets /dev/null as its standard input. Every log scenario checks that no probe error file remains. The fixture now has 59 scenarios.
